hypothesis: Y024's retained-placement churn benefit is causally attributable to using previously observed assignments, not merely the presence of nine-slot memory bookkeeping. With identical observed-only cache writes, turning off cache reads should increase churn.
source: Exact Y024 active-key, four-way collision and radius-two neighborhood generators, with eight episodes per seed and seven active motif keys of 16 total keys/cells.
arms: A0 matched-cache sham: allocate up to nine inactive entries and perform identical cache-update algorithm, but NEVER read cached assignment when deciding
A1 active cache use: same up-to-nine inactive entries and identical update algorithm, use only currently legal cached assignment as matching preference
frozen_policy: Both arms run the same deterministic augmenting-path matcher and same sort order when no legal preference. Cache writes are derived only from previous observed episodes; evaluator-only cumulative history cannot feed either policy.
primary: Returning-key assignment churn (assignment changes vs previous observed assignment for each key) on four disjoint heldout seeds. Record per-seed savings, episode cardinality, search-call totals, cache writes, cache-entry counts, and preference hits.
classification: CAUSAL_CACHE_READ_BENEFIT if A1 churn strictly lower than sham on every heldout seed, both maintain exact seven-key matching, and cache writes per-seed agree; MIXED if improvements and deteriorations occur; otherwise NO_CACHE_READ_BENEFIT. INVALID for differing cache-write counts, Hall-oracle mismatch, bounds violation, identity/determinism failure.
independent_checks: Exact predecessor and source Git identity before first use
Exhaustive Hall-deficiency oracle for seven-key matching per episode
No lookahead or evaluator-history access from either policy
deterministic repeated output and final full repository regression
claim_limit: Synthetic episodic placement only; does not establish learned semantic memory, cognition, original-data validation, or independent acceptance.
